clue.text: Sound broadcast?

definitions.meaning: a loud bang, such as a gunshot's crack
a news item read out on radio or television

explanation.definitionFit: A gun's bang is called its report, and a journalist's piece on the news is also a report.

clue.text: But it is not related to the forget-me-not!

definitions.text: But it is not related to the forget-me-not!

parts.words: But it is not related to the forget-me-not
parts.note: the herb traditionally stands for remembrance, as the forget-me-not does, yet botanically the two plants are no kin

explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia says this herb is 'for remembrance', the same meaning as the forget-me-not flower, though the plants are unrelated.

clue.text: Preliminary offer from claimant?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or preliminary
a tender is a formal offer or bid

explanation.surface: A claimant makes an opening offer before negotiations proper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is someone who lays claim to a throne or title.

clue.text: One is inclined to rush about excitedly

definitions.meaning: a sloping surface joining two levels
an old verb meaning to storm or rampage

explanation.definitionFit: A sloping way up is a ramp, and to ramp is also to charge about wildly, as in rampage.

clue.text: Turner's work, for example, the main view…

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. Turner painted many pictures of the sea
the main is an old word for the open ocean, so this is a view of the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: A painting or picture of the ocean, a genre Turner was famous for.

clue.text: Speak nonstop?

definitions.meaning: an ... train or coach runs without intermediate stops

explanation.definitionFit: To voice an idea is to express it, and a fast service that skips stations is an express.

clue.text: Low tar some consider dangerous

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, and one who goes low, under the waves, has a job some think risky

explanation.surface: Low-tar cigarettes are still considered a health hazard by some.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor serving on an underwater vessel, a tar who goes deep, in work many regard as perilous.

clue.text: Disappear, encased in gold, for so long

indicators.note: the word for disappear is held inside the symbol for gold, as if in a case

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to die away is to fade or vanish

explanation.surface: Something vanishes, locked up in gold, as a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads 'for so long'. 'encased in' puts DIE inside AU.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewells said on parting, French and English versions of goodbye.

clue.text: Team appearing one by one?

parts.note: a football or cricket side, whose number is written as the digit 1 beside another 1

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has this many players, and its numeral is two ones side by side.

clue.text: Prudence and Henry in Firth, perhaps

annotationWithheld.why: 'Prudence and Henry in Firth, perhaps': 'Prudence' defines THRIFT, but H (Henry) put in an anagram of FIRTH gives the letters FIRTHH, not THRIFT, and no other parse accounts for the extra T and the 'Henry'.
annotationWithheld.clue: Prudence and Henry in Firth, perhaps

clue.text: … of subject of mishap, set at sea

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and adrift, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Continuing the Turner scene: the painting depicts a disaster happening on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 4 across: the seascape is a view of this subject. 'at sea' rearranges MISHAP SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Turner painted steam-powered vessels, so such a ship is the subject of one of his sea views.

clue.text: Woman in veil to stay right. inside

indicators.note: the letter for right goes within the word for stay

parts.note: to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: A veiled woman is told to stay where she is.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman wearing a veil at the altar is typically one getting married.

clue.text: Huntsmen returning empty?

indicators.note: returning means the word for empty is read backwards

parts.note: to teem is to pour out or empty, as rain teems down

explanation.surface: Huntsmen come home with empty bags.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: huntsmen gathered before a hunt are a meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of riders and hounds before a fox hunt is called a meet.

clue.text: Turret Elia used to produce essays, etc?

indicators.note: the letters given are put to use and rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: Elia, the pen name of Charles Lamb, uses a turret as the setting for his writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia was the pen name under which Charles Lamb published his essays, which fits the surface. 'used to produce' rearranges TURRET ELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Written works such as essays, novels and poems make up the body of writing called by this name.

clue.text: Meandering in Rhode Island, you say?

definitions.meaning: said aloud, Rhode Island is 'road island', a circular island at a road junction

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a roundabout is a traffic circle, a raised island in the road. 'in' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Circuitous speech is roundabout, and a traffic circle in British English is a roundabout, an island in the road.

clue.text: Bloody tunic of old soldier.

parts.note: blood is red in colour
a tunic is a kind of coat or jacket

explanation.surface: A veteran's uniform jacket is stained with blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The British army once wore scarlet tunics, so its soldiers were called redcoats.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical British soldiers were known by the scarlet uniforms they wore.

clue.text: Exchange second character opening Macbeth

parts.note: Shakespeare's Macbeth opens with three witches on a heath

explanation.surface: An actor swaps the second part with the one who opens the Scottish play.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade one thing for another is to swap it, which is the same sense.

clue.text: The theatre for The Touchstone?

definitions.meaning: the ... Theatre is in London's Piccadilly Circus
a touchstone is a standard by which things are judged

explanation.definitionFit: A London West End theatre bears this name, and a standard for judging is a touchstone.

clue.text: Do campers use it for changing?

definitions.text: Do campers use it for changing?

parts.words: Do campers use it for changing
parts.note: bell-ringers ring changes, so a tent named after bells sounds like a place for changing

explanation.definitionFit: A conical tent held up by a single pole, shaped like a bell, used by campers.

clue.text: Quite a twist for cathedral architect to take on a 'small church

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A great architect makes an unexpected turn by taking on a little church commission.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent twist or pull is a wrench.

clue.text: Poisonous plant close to border

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so the word for close is added on after the word for border

parts.note: a hem is the edge or border of a cloth
to lock is to close fast

explanation.surface: A toxic weed grows near the edge of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemlock is a highly toxic umbellifer, famously used to execute Socrates.

clue.text: Late shift?

parts.note: a shift is also an old word for a woman's loose undergarment, put on late, at bedtime

explanation.definitionFit: A loose dress or undergarment once called a shift, worn for sleeping.

clue.text: Captain's first to wreck yacht — that is easily remembered

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for captain is taken
wrecking the boat scrambles its letters

explanation.surface: The captain is the first to run a yacht aground, which people won't forget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wreck' rearranges YACHT to give ATCHY. 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that sticks in the head is catchy.

clue.text: Monetary unit does some how include copper

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the symbol for copper
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A currency somehow manages to contain copper coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits the indicator over two lines as 'some-how'. It rearranges DOES to ESDO, and 'include' puts CU inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal before the euro.

clue.text: It grows up very slowly in a hollow

definitions.text: It grows up very slowly in a hollow

parts.words: It grows up very slowly in a hollow
parts.note: a mineral formation rising from a cave floor as dripping water deposits lime

explanation.definitionFit: A pillar of calcium carbonate built upwards from a cave floor over thousands of years.

clue.text: White poplar Jack Lee cut up

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

indicators.note: cut up means chopped about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jack Lee chops up a white poplar tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is another name for the white poplar tree.

clue.text: Softwood trade

explanation.definitionFit: Pine or fir planks are called deal, and to trade is to deal.

clue.text: Fare from France (using our lines, that is)

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the former UK railway network
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Food from France, sent over by British rail lines.
explanation.walkthrough: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railways until 1997, hence 'our lines' in a British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese, a food from France.

clue.text: Urticaria can be cured only from the inside

indicators.note: from the inside says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A skin rash is said to be curable only by internal treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is an old medical term for hives, a burning itchy skin condition.

clue.text: Else or Rose White turning out?

indicators.note: turning out signals the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Is the woman called Else, or does Rose White show up instead?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges ROSE WHITE. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise and else both mean in other circumstances, or if not.

clue.text: Leave behind what is done with and consume!

parts.note: something over is finished or done with
to take food or drink is to consume it

explanation.surface: An instruction to abandon what is finished and eat up.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass another vehicle and leave it behind is to overtake.

clue.text: Goober, an insignificant person in America

definitions.meaning: an American word for a groundnut
US slang for a small, unimportant person

explanation.definitionFit: Goober is a Southern US name for a groundnut, and in America an unimportant person is a peanut.
